# Typosquat corpus for rule MOAT-T5-001 (threat T5, issue #113).
#
# Each line is one case for TestTyposquatCorpus. The test builds a server of the
# given registry kind and runs the rule with the built-in popular list.
#
# Line format (single spaces between fields):
#   <expect> <registry> <name> [<related>]
#   expect:   ok  = no finding
#             hit = exactly one finding whose Related is <related>
#   registry: npm    = run as npx <name>
#             pypi   = run as uvx <name>
#             docker = run as docker run -i <name>
#             name   = only the server name, no package
#   related:  required for hit, absent for ok
# Lines that start with # and empty lines are ignored.
#
# Source: the ok names in the "real" groups are real packages. They were
# checked with a registry GET on npm, PyPI and Docker Hub on 2026-10-23. The
# one exception is mcp-server-tidb: it is a synthetic example from issue #113
# and it does not exist on npm or PyPI. The hit names and the names in the
# accepted-gap group are synthetic: they are made-up typos of names in
# rules/data/popular-servers.txt and are not real packages.
#
# The popular list is kind-aware (kind:name). A package is exact only when the
# list has the same kind and name. The same name on another registry is a hit
# with the plain popular name as related (the "other kind" groups below). A
# docker image under another owner with the same last component as a popular
# image is a namespace squat (dockerSquat in typosquat.go).
#
# An ok line for an accepted gap is a known false negative, not a bug. Do not
# "fix" it by adding it to a hit group. If the rule gets a fix for the gap,
# the fix must flip those lines to hit. In the same way, the hit lines in the
# accepted-false-positive group are known false positives: a fix must flip
# them to ok. The rules are closeDistance and dockerSquat in
# internal/rules/typosquat.go.

# --- ok: real npm packages ---
ok npm mcp-server-gcp

# --- ok: server name only (synthetic example from issue #113) ---
ok name mcp-server-gcp

# --- hit: one edit (typo or transposition) in the prefix or the tail ---
hit pypi mcp-server-fecth mcp-server-fetch
hit pypi mcp-server-fethc mcp-server-fetch
hit pypi mcp-server-fetcg mcp-server-fetch
hit pypi mcp-server-gti mcp-server-git
hit pypi mcp-server-sqlte mcp-server-sqlite
hit npm mcp-remot mcp-remote

hit npm mcp-sevrer-kubernetes mcp-server-kubernetes
hit npm mcp-server-kuberntees mcp-server-kubernetes

# --- hit: two edits (the shorter name has more than 8 runes and its part after the last shared separator has 5 runes or more) ---
hit pypi mcp-sever-fecth mcp-server-fetch
hit pypi mcp-sevrer-fecth mcp-server-fetch
hit npm mcp-sever-kubernets mcp-server-kubernetes
hit pypi mcp-server-fexxh mcp-server-fetch
hit npm mcp-server-kubernexez mcp-server-kubernetes

# --- hit: two runes appended to a popular name ---
hit pypi mcp-server-fetchxx mcp-server-fetch
hit npm mcp-remotejs mcp-remote
hit npm @evil/server-filesysxxm @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem
hit docker mcp/fetchxx mcp/fetch

# --- hit: two runes appended to a popular name whose last word is short ---
# The longer name starts with the whole popular name, so two edits count even
# when the part after the last separator has fewer than 5 runes.
hit pypi mcp-server-gitxx mcp-server-git
hit pypi mcp-server-timexx mcp-server-time
hit npm tavily-mcpjs tavily-mcp
hit npm firecrawl-mcpjs firecrawl-mcp

# --- hit: scope squats ---
hit npm @evil/server-filesystem @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem
hit npm @modelcontextprotocl/server-github @modelcontextprotocol/server-github
hit npm @modelcontextprotocol/server-githubb @modelcontextprotocol/server-github

# --- hit: popular name on another registry (related is the plain popular name) ---
hit npm mcp-server-fetch mcp-server-fetch
hit pypi firecrawl-mcp firecrawl-mcp

# --- hit: docker namespace squats (same last component, other owner or host) ---
hit docker evil/fetch mcp/fetch
hit docker ghcr.io/evil/github-mcp-server ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server
hit docker evil/github-mcp-server ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server
hit docker ghcr.io/mcp/fetch mcp/fetch

# --- hit: server name only and docker images ---
hit name mcp-server-fecth mcp-server-fetch
hit docker mcp/fecth mcp/fetch
hit docker mcp/fetchh mcp/fetch

# --- ok: accepted gaps (synthetic names, not real packages) ---
# Two edits that change a tail shorter than 5 runes after the last shared
# separator give no finding. The rule allows only one edit here, because a
# short tail cannot tell a typo from a different product (gcp against git).
# Popular names that end in a short word such as -mcp are in this gap too.
# This is a known false negative. A fix for it should flip these lines to hit.
# Runes only added at the end of the whole popular name are not in this gap
# (see the hit group for a short last word).
ok pypi mcp-server-gxx
ok pypi mcp-server-tixx
ok pypi mcp-server-gixx
ok npm tavily-mxx
ok npm firecrawl-mpx

# --- ok: accepted gap, docker (synthetic name, not a real image) ---
# A typo in the last component of a docker image gives no finding, because
# dockerSquat needs an equal last component and the edit distance of the whole
# name is too large. A last component under 5 runes is also skipped, but no
# popular docker entry has one today (mcp/git is not on the list), so there is
# no line for it. A fix should flip this line to hit.
ok docker evil/fecth

# --- ok: accepted gap, docker host without owner (known bypass) ---
# A registry host plus a bare name has no owner. The code skips it on purpose,
# but an attacker can use it to imitate mcp/fetch on another host. A fix must
# flip these lines to hit.
ok docker ghcr.io/fetch
ok docker localhost:5000/fetch

# --- ok: accepted gap, docker image named like an npm or PyPI package ---
# A docker image whose last component equals a popular npm or PyPI name is not
# compared: only docker entries are used for docker images. A fix must flip
# this line to hit.
ok docker evil/mcp-server-fetch

# --- hit: accepted false positive (synthetic name, not a real package) ---
# Two runes added at the end of a popular name count even after a short last
# word, so a real product that extends a popular name this way gets a finding.
# mcp-server-gitee was not on npm or PyPI on 2026-10-23. A fix for this should
# flip the line to ok.
hit pypi mcp-server-gitee mcp-server-git

# --- hit: accepted false positive, popular name on another registry ---
# mcp-server-git is a real npm package (checked with a registry GET on
# 2026-10-23). The popular list has the PyPI mcp-server-git, so the npm package
# with the same name gets a finding. A user can add the server to the ignore
# file. A fix for this should flip the line to ok.
hit npm mcp-server-git mcp-server-git

# --- hit: accepted false positive, private docker mirror (synthetic name) ---
# A company registry that mirrors mcp/fetch under its own host looks like a
# namespace squat. A user can add the server to the ignore file. A fix for this
# should flip the line to ok.
hit docker harbor.corp/mcp/fetch mcp/fetch
